newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Proton, Hicom half-year in-line - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Proton, Hicom half-year in-line - analysts.

text.p: The half-year results of Malaysian car maker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) and its auto distributor parent Hicom Holdings Bhd were in line with expectations, analysts said on Wednesday.

"The pre-tax profit was generally in line with our expectations. It should have a minimal impact on the share price," said Choo Swee Kee, auto analyst at equities research house Vickers Ballas in Kuala Lumpur.

"The results for Hicom include the acquisition of Automotive Corporation (a distributor of Isuzu vehicles), and United Straits Fuso (a distributor of Mitsubishi vehicles)," said John Engle, managing director of equities research house HG Asia in Kuala Lumpur.
Hicom assembles and distributes commercial and industrial vehicles, manufactures cement, and is in construction.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, Proton said its pre-tax profit for the six months ended September 30, 1996 was 454.29 million ringgit ($179.9 million), compared to 127.29 million ringgit for the same period in 1995.

Hicom, which owns a 29.6 percent stake in Proton, announced that its pre-tax profit for the six months to September 30, 1996 was 407.92 million ringgit, compared to 180.09 million ringgit for the same period in 1995.
Hicom described the half-year results as "commendable", adding that "double-digit growths (were) recorded by companies in the automotive and property and construction sectors".

"The yen is going to have far less of an impact in the second half, than in the first half. Most of the impact will come from efficiency gains and lower cost of component parts," said Engle, referring to both Hicom and Proton.
Analysts had said in October they expected Proton's half-year pre-tax profit for the six months to September 30, 1996 to be roughly equivalent to the whole of the 1995 financial year.
"Proton achieved its full year pre-tax profits for the previous year in their first half," Engle said.

"In the second half, their continued strong performance will depend on their sustaining unit sales. They probably will be able to do this. If they maintain the momentum of their unit sales they will be OK," said Engle.
Hicom's management remained optimistic about the second half-year results.
"We expect results in the second half to be comparable to the first half," Mohd. Saleh Sulong, group managing director of Hicom, told reporters after announcing the results.
Proton shares closed unchanged at 16.10 ringgit on Wednesday, while Hicom was up 30 cents to 7.25 ringgit.
